book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

indicators.note: one word goes on the outside of another, wrapping around it

parts.note: frenzied and frantic
zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A calm gardener lets nothing frantic happen outside among the plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Manioc is another name for cassava, a tropical plant grown for its starchy root.

parts.note: to own something is to have it
nickname of Chelsea (and other clubs) who play in blue

explanation.surface: A fan whose club has just lost is told to own up to feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea, the London football club, are known as the Blues.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the blues is an idiom for feeling sad or low, which is being depressed.

parts.note: surface reading: firm proof, or proof of what concrete is like
setter's reading: concrete is a set, solid material, and evidence is made of information

explanation.walkthrough: Concrete means definite, but the question mark nods to the building material, which is famously solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard facts are definite, indisputable information, exactly what concrete evidence means.

parts.note: Vi is the usual short form of the name Violet

indicators.note: read as re-moved, moved about again, so the letters change places

parts.note: the name taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people, Violet and Saul, take away an eye-related item.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often shorten a first name to its nickname, here Violet to Vi.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic and visual are both adjectives relating to sight and the eye.

parts.note: surface reading: recently, so someone has disapproved of late
setter's reading: as the late, that is, someone who has died

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lately' seems to mean recently, but it points to the late, the dead, whose imagined disapproval is the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone is said to turn in their grave when something done after their death would have appalled them.

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, enclosed by it

parts.note: before the expected time

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected outcome, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged and placed inside

explanation.surface: A gale sprang up unexpectedly early.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly is a wind blowing from the east.

clue.text: Great Scottish resort changes direction at the end

indicators.note: the final compass point is swapped for a different compass point

parts.note: Largs is a seaside town on the Firth of Clyde

explanation.surface: A fine Scottish holiday town alters its route at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The S (south) closing the town's name becomes E (east). Largs is a resort on Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Great and large both mean big in size.

parts.note: surface reading: hardly managing to turn up
setter's reading: in a bare way, uncovering, and showing up means revealing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' seems to mean only just, but here it means nakedly; showing up is revealing rather than arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposing means laying bare or uncovering, and also showing someone up by revealing their faults.

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A lama is a Buddhist monk or spiritual teacher in Tibet, a kind of priest.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a thing written again, a rewriting
second meaning: an official edict, originally a Roman emperor's written reply

explanation.surface: An official order is being redrafted.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a written-out second version and a formal ruling or edict issued by an authority.

clue.text: Go round stream in Scotland with inflammation

parts.note: a path or road that winds goes round and about
burn is the Scottish word for a stream

explanation.surface: A walker circles a Highland brook and comes away with a sore.
explanation.definitionFit: Windburn is skin reddened and irritated by exposure to the wind, a form of inflammation.

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece sitting on another is simply placed before it
something strange is out of the ordinary, so the letters next to it come out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A critic finds some love poetry very odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very strange' reads as one phrase, but 'Very' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever so is an informal intensifier meaning extremely, the same as very.

indicators.note: transporting carries things off elsewhere, so these letters are moved into new places

parts.note: the two words supply all ten letters

explanation.surface: A trader depends on carrying goods by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean liner is a large passenger vessel, a kind of ship.

clue.text: Lulu loses half 16, it is clear

indicators.note: losing half means one of the name's two equal halves is dropped

parts.note: the singer's name, which is cut in two
a cross-reference to the answer at 16 across, money; a cent is a piece of money

explanation.surface: The singer Lulu is somehow halved alongside a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 points to the answer of 16 across, MONEY, and a cent is one example of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucent means shining or translucent, letting light through, so it is a literary word for clear.

parts.note: surface reading: a punch landed from the side
setter's reading: blow as what air currents do

explanation.walkthrough: A blow sounds like a punch, but the question mark hints that wind blows too.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosswind is one blowing across the direction of travel, so it hits from the side.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: felt is a fabric, a type of cloth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Felt' reads as a verb, but it is the noun for pressed wool cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for cloth such as felt and an adjective meaning significant or relevant.

clue.text: Notes perhaps, one is in my possession

indicators.note: the number sits within the possessive word, held as if owned

parts.note: taken as written, the outer letters
taken as written, placed inside

explanation.surface: Someone owns a single banknote, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in my possession' reads as ownership; here it places one inside my.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes are one example of money, which the word 'perhaps' signals.

clue.text: Swallow, visitor from outer space, a disciplinarian!

parts.note: the martin is a bird of the swallow family
ET, the extra-terrestrial of the film

explanation.surface: A list of a bird, an alien and a strict boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb meaning gulp, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a person who insists on strict obedience, a stern disciplinarian.

indicators.note: something amongst others is surrounded by them, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: the American Central Intelligence Agency
an ass is a silly person

explanation.surface: A double agent or idiot has been planted among intelligence officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb about planting a spy, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassia is a genus of tropical shrubs and trees, one source of a cinnamon-like spice, so a plant.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an adjective, corresponding or in keeping with something

explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondent' looks like a noun for a letter-writer, but here it is the adjective meaning corresponding.
explanation.definitionFit: Responsive means replying or reacting, and dictionaries also give it the older sense of corresponding to something.

clue.text: Some actors in one Shakespearean part

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is used

parts.note: the run of letters across the words

explanation.surface: Several actors share a single Shakespeare role.
explanation.definitionFit: Orsino, Duke of Illyria, is a character in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, so a role an actor plays.

clue.text: Do nothing with five ducks first in witchcraft!

indicators.note: these come first, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O
taken as written
zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A lazy sorcerer idles while five ducks feature in a spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do nothing' reads as idling but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Voodoo is a religion of Caribbean origin associated with spells and magic, hence witchcraft.

clue.text: Flat bunks — they're the very thing

parts.note: bunks are a kind of beds
'that's it' means that is the very thing wanted

explanation.surface: An estate agent says the bunk beds in a flat are perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedsit is British for a one-room rented flat used for both sleeping and living.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a small rented flat, a single room serving as bedroom and sitting room.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to have a nose (sniff) is to smell
second meaning: a small silvery fish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Had a nose for fish' reads as a talent for finding fish; it is two meanings joined by 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Smelt is the British past tense of smell and also the name of a small edible fish.

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, to grow higher
a wood is a small forest

explanation.surface: Trees in a forest grew into lumber.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosewood is a dark, fragrant hardwood used for furniture and instruments, a type of timber.

clue.text: Most of team come from Ireland

indicators.note: most of a thing is all but its final part, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Hibernian, often called Hibs, is an Edinburgh football club

explanation.surface: Most of a side's players are Irish-born.
explanation.walkthrough: Hibernian is a Scottish football club from Edinburgh; any team of the right length would do, which makes this one hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernia is the Latin name the Romans gave to Ireland, still used poetically.

parts.note: surface reading: the most drawn-out walkout by workers
setter's reading: the hour when a clock chimes the most strokes, twelve

explanation.walkthrough: Strike suggests industrial action, but it is a clock striking; at twelve it strikes most often.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is twelve o'clock, when a striking clock sounds twelve times, its longest run of chimes.

clue.text: Unusually hot old-age lot to be welcomed without reservation

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the following letters appear in an uncommon order

parts.note: all twelve letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Pensioners enjoying an unseasonably warm day greet it gladly.
explanation.definitionFit: All to the good is an idiom for a wholly beneficial thing, one that can be welcomed without any reservation.
